verses.text: That night the king couldn't sleep. He ordered the royal chronicles brought in and read aloud to him.
The records showed that Mordecai had reported Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the entrance and had plotted against King Ahasuerus.
The king asked, "What honor or recognition did Mordecai receive for this?" His attendants replied, "Nothing was done for him."
The king asked, "Who's in the courtyard?" Haman had just come into the outer court of the palace to ask the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows he'd prepared for him.
The king's attendants answered, "Haman is in the courtyard." The king said, "Let him in."
When Haman came in, the king asked him, "What should be done for the man the king wants to honor?" Haman thought, "Who would the king want to honor more than me?"
He answered the king, "For the man the king wants to honor,
bring out a robe the king himself has worn and a horse the king rides, with a royal crown on its head.

Put the robe and horse in the care of one of the king's highest officials. Have him dress the man the king wants to honor and lead him on horseback through the city square, announcing, 'This is what happens to the man the king wants to honor!'"
The king told Haman, "Hurry. Take the robe and horse, just as you said, and do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Carry out everything you've suggested."
So Haman took the robe and horse, dressed Mordecai, and led him on horseback through the city square. He announced in front of him, "This is what happens to the man the king wants to honor!"
Mordecai went back to the king's gate. Haman hurried home in mourning with his head covered.

Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends what had happened. His advisers and Zeresh told him, "If Mordecai is Jewish and you've already begun to fall before him, you won't get the better of him. You're sure to fall before him."
While they were still talking, the king's eunuchs arrived and hurried Haman to Esther's banquet.
